meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: at the end of the established pay period
facts.summary: Washington: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due at the end of the established pay period.
facts.evidence_quote: (2) When any employee shall cease to work for an employer, whether by discharge or by voluntary withdrawal, the wages due him or her on account of his or her employment shall be paid to him or her at the end of the established pay period
facts.source_title: RCW 49.48.010, Payment of wages due to employee ceasing work

facts.value: at the end of the established pay period
facts.summary: Washington: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due at the end of the established pay period.
facts.evidence_quote: (2) When any employee shall cease to work for an employer, whether by discharge or by voluntary withdrawal, the wages due him or her on account of his or her employment shall be paid to him or her at the end of the established pay period
facts.source_title: RCW 49.48.010, Payment of wages due to employee ceasing work

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Washington basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $17.13.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $17.13 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 Premium pay not applicable to employees who request compensating time off in lieu of premium pay. The minimum wage is adjusted annually based on a set formula.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Washington independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): No
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Washington new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of hire date
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Within 20 days of hire date
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Washington: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Monthly.
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Washington is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Washington 2026 new employer UI rate: 115% of the average rate for the employer's industry, with a 1% minimum.
facts.evidence_quote: We will assign you a tax rate based on your industry. For 2026, you will pay 115% of the average rate for all businesses in your industry. Federal law sets the minimum rate at 1%.
facts.source_title: How we determine tax rates (Washington Employment Security Department)
facts.notes: No single numeric default; enter your assigned rate in the calculator. WA.ui.rate_range is the experience portion; the flat social tax (capped at 1.22%) and the employment administration fund (0.02% to 0.03%) are added on top.

facts.summary: Washington experience-rated UI tax rates range from 0.00% to 5.40%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. This range is the experience-rated portion only. ESD adds a flat social tax (currently capped at 1.22%) and an employment administration fund fee (0.02% to 0.03%) (https://esd.wa.gov/employer-requirements/unemployment-taxes/how-we-determine-tax-rates).

facts.summary: Washington state unemployment taxable wage base: $78,200 per employee.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance

facts.summary: Washington workers' compensation agency website as linked by U.S. DOL OWCP: http://www.lni.wa.gov/
facts.source_title: State Workers' Compensation Officials (U.S. DOL OWCP)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Office of Workers' Compensation Programs

facts.value: Yes: private workers' comp coverage is not allowed; buy from L&I or be a certified self-insured employer
facts.summary: Washington: Yes: private workers' comp coverage is not allowed; buy from L&I or be a certified self-insured employer.
facts.evidence_quote: Washington State does not allow private workers' compensation coverage. You must purchase your coverage from L&I or be a certified self-insured employer.
facts.source_title: Do I Need a Workers' Comp Account? (Washington L&I)
facts.source_publisher: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries
